question.text: Among the following species <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> the number of species showing diamagnetism is

solution.text:
The molecules with unpaired electrons are paramagnetic and molecules with all electrons paired are diamagnetic. In general molecules with an even number of electrons (except 10 and 16 electrons) are diamagnetic

N214e- diamagnetic

N2+13e- paramagnetic 

N2-15e-paramagnetic

N22-16e- paramagnetic

O216e-paramagnetic

O2+15e-paramagnetic

O2-17e-paramagnetic

O22-18e-diamagnetic
